title: Samantha and the Little Lost Bunny
author: Dady Fredy
subtitle: A Bedtime Story by Dady Fredy
dedication: For Samantha — who always has room in her hands for someone small.

lines: Step by step, through the forest so deep,
We'll take little Ivana home before sleep!
closing: Step by step, through the forest so deep,
Ivana is home — and Samantha's asleep.

pages.title: Samantha and the Little Lost Bunny
pages.subtitle: A Bedtime Story by Dady Fredy
pages.dedication: For Samantha — who always has room in her hands for someone small.

lines: When the sun was all golden and sinking down low,
Dady Fredy said, "Shoes on, my love — let's go!"
So hand in big hand, down the path they did stride,
To the whispering forest, so green and so wide.
The pine trees stood tall and the ferns waved hello,
A woodpecker knocked, and a stream gurgled slow.
"Shh," whispered Dady, "now listen — be still…"
And they heard a small sniffle from under the hill.
Behind a big mushroom, all spotty and red,
Sat a teeny-tiny bunny with a leaf on her head!
Her fur was as white as a dandelion puff,
And she trembled and sniffled — her day had been tough.
"Hello there," Samantha said, kneeling down low,
"Why so sad, little bunny? Where do you need to go?"
"I'm Ivana," she sniffled. "I followed a bee,
Now I'm lost, and my mama can't find little me!"
Samantha held out her two hands like a cup,
And Ivana hopped in — she was light as a pup.
"Don't worry," Samantha said, "soon you will see —
We'll find your home, Ivana, my Dady and me!"
Dady Fredy knelt down by a puddle of mud:
"Look — tiny paw prints! Little hop, little thud!"
They followed the prints past a log and a stone,
Past a hedgehog asleep, all curled up on his own.
An owl in an oak tree called, "Hoo? Who goes there?"
"We're helping Ivana! Is her mama somewhere?"
The owl blinked her big eyes and turned round her head:
"Go past the old willow, to the clover-patch bed."
Now the forest grew darker, the shadows grew long,
And the crickets began their soft evening song.
Samantha held tight to her Dady's warm hand —
Then a thousand small fireflies lit up the land!
The fireflies twinkled a path through the night,
To the old weeping willow, all silver and bright.
They pushed back its branches, like curtains of green —
And there was the loveliest meadow they'd seen!
A meadow of clover, all moonlit and sweet,
And a rabbit stood calling, up high on her feet:
"Ivana! Ivana! Oh, where can you be?"
"MAMA!" squeaked Ivana. "It's me! It's ME!"
Ivana jumped down with a hop and a bound,
And snuggled her mama — at last she was found!
Her brothers and sisters came tumbling to see,
And they wiggled their noses with bunny-hop glee!
"Thank you," said Mama, "you're kind and you're true.
You brought my girl home — so this is for you."
A four-leaf clover, so tiny and green:
The luckiest present Samantha had seen!
"Come back and visit!" Ivana called out,
With a flick of her tail and a twitch of her snout.
Samantha blew kisses and waved her goodbye,
As the fireflies led them back under the sky.
"I'm so proud," whispered Dady, "of you, my brave one —
You helped someone small till the helping was done.
When someone feels frightened and lost in the night,
A kind, gentle heart is the very best light."
Samantha was sleepy, her steps slow and small,
So Dady Fredy lifted her up, up, up tall.
On his shoulders she rode past the trees and the stream,
With her clover held tight, almost lost in a dream.
Now the clover is tucked by her pillow just right,
And off in the forest, Ivana sleeps tight.
Two little girls dreaming beneath the same moon…
Goodnight, my Samantha. Sweet dreams — see you soon.
Goodnight, Samantha.
Goodnight, anak.
